title: Instrumental 2: Feminine -ой / -ей
description: Feminine instrumental endings: -а → -ой, -я → -ей. Drilled with пишет ручкой, интересуется музыкой, гордится тётей.
descriptionRussian: Окончания творительного падежа в женском роде: -а → -ой, -я → -ей.
intro: Feminine endings, and a spelling rule you have met before: after certain consonants an unstressed о is written е instead. The adjective book used the same rule to explain хорошее. It costs you nothing once you know it is there, and here it decides which of two endings you write.
rules: Feminine nouns ending in -а swap the final vowel for -ой: мама → мамой, книга → книгой, работа → работой.
Feminine nouns ending in -я swap the final vowel for -ей: неделя → неделей, тётя → тётей, кухня → кухней.

Spelling rule (hushers ж, ш, щ, ч, ц): when the ending is UNSTRESSED after one of these letters, write -ей not -ой. Examples: Маша → Ма́шей (stem stress), крыша → кры́шей, учительница → учи́тельницей. When the ending IS stressed, -ой stays: душа → душо́й, свеча → свечо́й.
The verb гордиться (to be proud of) takes the instrumental directly: гордиться кем / чем.

Like пользоваться and интересоваться from L1, гордиться belongs to a small family of A2 verbs that take the instrumental directly with no preposition (all three end in -ся, but you don't need to know the term 'reflexive' to use them).
Feminine nouns ending in soft -ь (площадь, ночь, дверь) take a different ending -ью; those get their own dedicated lesson at L7.
examples: Маша пишет ручкой. (Masha writes with a pen.) ручка → ручкой.
Лена интересуется музыкой. (Lena is interested in music.) музыка → музыкой.
Соня интересуется математикой. (Sonya is interested in math.) математика → математикой.
Маша пользуется кухней. (Masha uses the kitchen.) кухня → кухней.
Антон гордится тётей. (Anton is proud of his aunt.) тётя → тётей.

items.hint: Recall yesterday: what's the masculine hard-consonant instrumental ending?
items.explanation: Warm-up from Lesson 1. The pencil is the instrument: masculine hard consonant + -ом → карандашом. Today we move to feminine, but the role is the same.

items.hint: Ручка is feminine -а. What does -а change to in the instrumental?
items.explanation: Ручка ends in -а: feminine. The instrumental swaps -а for -ой → ручкой.

items.hint: Интересоваться takes the instrumental. Музыка ends in -а; what's the ending?
items.explanation: Интересоваться (to be interested in) takes its complement in the instrumental: интересоваться чем. Музыка is feminine -а: -а → -ой → музыкой.

items.hint: Same construction as Q1.3. Apply the feminine -а rule again.
Кухня ends in soft -я. What replaces -я in the instrumental?
items.explanation: Кухня is feminine -я: -я → -ей → кухней. The soft ending stays soft, paralleling the masculine soft pattern (учитель → учителем) from yesterday.

items.promptEnglish: Anton is proud of his aunt.
items.hint: Гордиться is a new verb that takes the instrumental. Тётя is feminine -я.
items.explanation: Гордиться (to be proud of) takes the instrumental: гордиться кем. Тётя is feminine -я: -я → -ей → тётей.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Ложка is feminine -а. The verb пользоваться takes the instrumental: -а → -ой → ложкой.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha is very proud of her older sister.
errorCorrection.explanation: Гордиться governs the instrumental: гордиться кем. Сестра is feminine -а, so the instrumental is сестрой. Сестры is the genitive, which a learner picks because English 'proud of' feels possessive, but Russian гордиться takes the instrumental, not the genitive.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton is very proud of his grandmother.
errorCorrection.explanation: Гордиться governs the instrumental: гордиться кем. Бабушка is feminine -а, so the instrumental swaps -а for -ой: бабушкой. Бабушку is the accusative, which a learner uses by treating 'proud of grandma' as a direct object, but гордиться never takes the accusative.

errorCorrection.sentence: Родители гордятся Машой и её успехами.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Her parents are proud of Masha and her achievements.
errorCorrection.explanation: Маша ends in the husher ш, and after a husher an UNSTRESSED instrumental ending is written -ей, not -ой: Машей (the stress stays on Ма́-). Машой applies the regular feminine -ой without checking the husher rule. The -ой ending survives only when it is stressed (душа → душо́й).

minimalPairs.explanation: The pen is the INSTRUMENT, so it goes in the instrumental: ручкой. The nominative ручка would only mark a subject ('Ручка на столе.' / 'The pen is on the table.').
Пользоваться takes the instrumental: кухней. The nominative кухня would mark a subject ('Кухня большая.' / 'The kitchen is big.'), not the thing being used.

reviewVocab.definition: to be interested in (takes instrumental: интересоваться чем)
to be proud of (takes instrumental: гордиться кем / чем)
feminine gender (nouns ending in -а or -я; in the instrumental they take -ой or -ей)
